BT9dPL0zK$?71xx(1w_j.text:
The second step is more complicated, as it is involved in the automatic alignment of players and the improved zoom feature for when a player wins the game. This step can be omitted in AY-minigames that don't require the screen to zoom in like the Marble Madness games.

This step is skipped if the players are already aligned by this step previously in order to make loading the game more efficient. However, this process will still execute if the scale of any player is newly modified.

m0(C!O*_#06:u]FiLQSG.text: The second step of preparing the updated zoom feature creates clones of the green "Upper Alignment" line until it has as many clones as there are players in the game. Each line is assigned to a player number of a player in the game and sets its y-position to the top of the player's sprite with the respective player number. Each line's y-position is added to the "ModifiedScaleHelper" list which would be used in the next step.

`T.Q*p^8MUAor!ILv8jH.text: The third step creates clones of the blue "Scale Proportion" line until it has as many clones as there are players in the game. Each line is assigned to a player number of a player in the game and sets its y-position to an amplified version of the respective y-position in the "ModifiedScaleHelper" list.

Y{gzHMLd_@N*Q^m728UC.text: This process simply nudges all alignment lines and aligned players proportionally to the bottom of the screen so taller players can be supported by the game without stage boundaries messing everything up.

KGNM?(MVhr(2P_P~:74D.text:
With the "Scale Proportion" lines in place, the final step in preparing the updated zoom feature can commence. Each player individually will grow with only their respective "Scale Proportion" line showing. Once the player touches their line, their "Modified Scale" variable will be set to their current size, they will revert to their normal assigned size, and the process will move on to the next player. This repeats until all players have been checked.

The "Modified Scale" variable will be used in scaling the player proportionally to the zoom that occurs when they win the game. Previously, the zoom was not proportional between the players and everything else, which would cause players with small sprites in the costume editor to become gigantic when winning.

This entire process also cannot run without screen refresh, as running it without screen refresh will severely lag the project during the loading process and potentially cause things to break.

HIT STATES:
0: 50% chance to deal 1 damage. Used only by small marbles released from the soon-to-be-added multi marble.

1: The default hit state for if no hit state is assigned. Always deals 1 damage. Apart from small marbles, it is likely that all other marbles that V3 introduces will have this hit state.

2: Deals 2 damage. Used by large marbles.

3: Deals 3 damage. Used by speedy marbles.

4. Deals 1 damage and teleports the player to a random location on the platform. Used by warp marbles.

5. KOs the player. Used by spiked marbles.

6. Deals 1 damage and pauses the player in place until they are hit by another marble. Used by pause marbles.

g2E:QQCr6[v^V.gji`?:.text:
You can add your character's costumes and sound clips to add your character to the game!

If you set the "Seconds per run frame:" to an empty input, the interval will be faster than 0 seconds.

You can also add as many Ouch voice clips and footstep sounds, just make sure to apply the changes to this custom block above.

If your character's costumes are too big or too small compared to the grey box costumes provided, you can use the size input to adjust the size of your character without effecting any hitbox sizes.

Make sure to add some color to make sure they have been paused by a pause marble!

Make sure to change the name from [ NAME HERE ] or else they won't participate in the game!
